deities: Lord Shiva (separate idol in the temple)
festivals: Ram Navami (Shobha Yatra - grand annual procession with decorated chariot of Rama, Sita and Lakshman, Ramayana tableaus, mangal-kalash and fireworks)

history.dynasty: None (private temple built and administered by the Poddar family board of trustees)
history.summary: Sri Poddareshwar Ram Mandir, on Central Avenue Road near the Nagpur railway station, was built in 1923 by Shri Jamnadhar Poddar, a businessman of the famous Poddar family of Bisau, Rajasthan; 'Poddareshwar' means the Lord of the Poddar family, and one account says he erected it in memory of his departed son (verify). Constructed of marble and sandstone with ornate carvings, it houses the Ram Parivar - Rama, Sita, Lakshman and Hanuman - along with a Shiva idol, and is often called the pride of Nagpur. Believers hold that a visit here grants peace of mind. Its signature event is the Ram Navami Shobha Yatra, a grand procession with a flower-decked chariot, Ramayana tableaus and fireworks that draws thousands. The temple premises include the Jamnadhar Poddar Dharamshala, which offers free stay for devotees, and the temple and dharamshala are administered by a board of trustees from the Poddar family.

name: Sri Poddareshwar Ram Mandir
town_description: Nagpur, in north-eastern Maharashtra on the Nag River, is the state's second capital and its geographic centre - the Zero Mile Stone marks the centre of India here. Known as the 'Orange City' for its citrus trade, it is a major commercial, educational and transport hub, home to Deekshabhoomi (Dr. Ambedkar's historic Buddhist conversion site), Sitabuldi Fort and the famous Ramtek temple about 50 km away. The Sri Poddareshwar Ram Mandir sits in the Santra Market/Bajaria area on Central Avenue, a short walk from Nagpur Junction.

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur (approx. 8-9 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Nagpur Junction (approx. 1-1.5 km - a short walk via the station's east side or a quick auto ride), well connected across India.
travel.road: On Central Avenue Road (CA Road) at Santra Market, Bajaria, opp. Mayo Hospital, near Ram Jhula; easily reached by auto-rickshaw, taxi and city buses from anywhere in Nagpur.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Ram Navami is the grandest time, with the famous Shobha Yatra drawing thousands.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Generally 6:00 AM to evening (verify - sources differ: one lists 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM, another 6:00 AM to 9:30 PM daily). No entry fee; at least 30 minutes for a visit.
